gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

gaps.sentence: Never before that afternoon ___ so many goals been scored in one match.
gaps.explanation: 'Never before that afternoon' fixes the reference in the past: had so many goals been scored.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than the rumours started.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been signed than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
gaps.explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

gaps.sentence: Try ___ she might, she couldn't restart the engine.
gaps.explanation: 'Try as somebody might' — fixed concessive inversion.

gaps.sentence: Nowhere ___ you find a better example of Gothic architecture.
At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.
